add.issue.name: Disabling a plugin leaves its UI module linked in the shell tree

edit.description.md:
`_aphotic_plugin_relink_all_ui_modules` (Configs/.local/lib/aphotic/commands/cmd_plugin.sh:1147) links a module for every enabled plugin and `continue`s past disabled ones, so disabling never removes the link.

Live evidence: `~/.config/quickshell/aphotic/modules/plugins/gameLauncher` still exists although game-launcher was disabled on 2026-10-08 (recorded in ~/.local/state/aphotic/changes.log).

Fix: the relink pass should also remove the module link for a plugin that is installed but disabled, and for one that is no longer installed. Removing a plugin's UI tree must leave nothing behind.

Found while tracing the plugin-registry wipe (see the atomic state write PR #311).

add.issue.name: A workspace surface counts as present even when its component cannot load

edit.description.md:
`WorkspaceKeybind.wanted` is `PluginRegistry.surfacesFor("workspace").length > 0`, computed from the registry alone, so it does not care whether the component exists on disk.

Live evidence: `dev-ports` is enabled and declares `[ui.workspace]` with `requires_layer = "dev"`, and there is no `modules/plugins/devPorts` in the tree (the module link is what the other ticket covers). The count is non-zero, so the combo is bound (`hyprctl binds -j` shows `modmask=65 __lua 86 [Toggle plugin workspace]`), and the plane opens with nothing loadable inside it, rendering as "No plugin surfaces".

This is what reads as SUPER+SHIFT+W not working. The bind is present; the plane is empty.

Fix direction: the shell should know a surface is unloadable (module missing, load failed) and not count it, and the plane should name the surface that failed instead of showing the empty state.
